section_summary: This section (pages 73-152) comprises State Department records from late 1945 through early 1947 concerning post-war Japanese economic affairs, industrial capacity, and Allied occupation policies. It includes field interrogations of North China Development Company officials regarding wartime resource exploitation, correspondence on trade programs and reparations removals, public inquiries regarding Japanese economic conditions, and the complete first issue of SCAP's monthly bulletin 'Japanese Economic Statistics' (September 1946). Also included are confidential assessments by Political Adviser George Atcheson on Japan's severe economic crisis and legal analyses regarding the deconcentration and dissolution of the Zaibatsu.

subfiles.about: Interrogation of Shuo Tsuda regarding the corporate organization, mining activities, and operating affiliates of the North China Development Company.
subfiles.summary: Interrogation covers Tsuda's career, structure of Kitashina Kaihatsu's 64 operating affiliates, mining enterprises, and wartime Japanese employment in North China.
subfiles.title: Interrogation of Tsuda, Shuo (Vice President, North China Development Company)

subfiles.about: Interrogation of Michio Izawa covering geological surveys, industrial machinery manufacturing, security operations, and the debt structure of the North China Development Company.
subfiles.summary: Izawa details geological surveys for coking coal and iron ore, machinery production in Tientsin, and reliance on Japanese technicians. He describes holding company finances, bank borrowings, currency depreciation, and total corporate indebtedness.
subfiles.title: Interrogation of Izawa, Michio (Advisor and Research Chief, North China Development Company)

subfiles.about: Interrogation of Hisahi Mitsuyuki concerning intelligence coordination, propaganda, railway guards, and labor security in North China.
subfiles.summary: Mitsuyuki discusses intelligence flow from the Japanese Embassy, military secondments, railway guard forces, and the Keiro Hombu security headquarters.
subfiles.title: Interrogation of Mitsuyuki, Hisahi (Propaganda and Publicity Chief, North China Transportation Company)

subfiles.about: Department of State acknowledgment of Mackenzie's submission of interrogation transcripts of Japanese personnel in North China.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of Mackenzie's North China interrogation transcripts for State Department permanent files and declines proposed mission to Russia.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Albert H. Mackenzie

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a proposed cable to SCAP summarizing British comments on Japan's 1946 export-import program.
subfiles.summary: Transmits proposed cable to SCAP regarding British comments and commercial interests in Japan's 1946 import-export program.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. H. Hilldring to Major General Oliver P. Echols

subfiles.about: Confirmation of State Department concurrence on draft cable to SCAP regarding British comments on trade programs.
subfiles.summary: Confirms telephone notification of State Department concurrence on cable regarding British comments on SCAP's trade program.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from P. P. Claxton to Colonel Chard

subfiles.about: Recommendation to dispatch proposed cable to SCAP regarding British trade comments, Egyptian cotton, and textile machinery.
subfiles.summary: Recommends forwarding cable to SCAP addressing British trade comments, Egyptian cotton imports, and textile machinery part exports.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Mr. Easton to Mr. Gross

subfiles.about: Proposed draft cable instructing SCAP on handling British comments, Egyptian raw cotton, and Indian textile parts requests.
subfiles.summary: Presents draft cable to SCAP addressing British trade comments, Egyptian cotton requirements, and textile machinery parts for India.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Roswell H. Whitman to General J. H. Hilldring

subfiles.about: Evaluation of synthetic oil and synthetic rubber facilities regarding domestic economic needs and availability for reparations.
subfiles.summary: SCAP evaluates synthetic oil and rubber plants, recommending release of rubber facilities for reparations while retaining fertilizer equipment.
subfiles.title: Telegram 64280 from SCAP Tokyo to War Department

subfiles.about: Transmittal of copies of interim reparations removal directives and cable reference lists to SCAP's political adviser.
subfiles.summary: Transmits interim reparations removal directives and dispatch cable lists to SCAP's Political Adviser office.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Norman J. Meiklejohn

subfiles.about: Cross-reference certification replacing unreturned yellow action copy of telegram with white record copy in permanent files.
subfiles.summary: Records replacement of missing yellow action copy with white record copy of telegram for permanent central files.
subfiles.title: Document Replacement Sheet for File 894.50/8-2346

subfiles.about: Reporting terms of agreement with Australian economic mission representative for raw silk export from Kure to Australia.
subfiles.summary: Reports agreement with Australian representative to export 300 raw silk bales from Kure on S/S Merkur.
subfiles.title: Telegram CM-IN-5196 from SCAP Tokyo to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Citizen inquiry requesting economic, geographic, foreign trade, and tariff information on Japan.
subfiles.summary: Inquires about available State Department publications covering pre-war and post-war Japanese foreign trade, tariffs, and economic data.
subfiles.title: Letter from Lawrence Miller to Department of State

subfiles.about: Department response directing Lawrence Miller to published works and the New York Public Library for economic data on Japan.
subfiles.summary: Advises Miller that no comprehensive department summary exists and suggests relevant reference volumes in the New York library.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Lawrence Miller

subfiles.about: Comprehensive statistical compilation of Japanese production, mining, agriculture, trade, labor wages, prices, and financial accounts.
subfiles.from: GHQ, SCAP, Economic and Scientific Section, Research and Statistics Division
subfiles.summary: This inaugural statistical bulletin compiled by SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section details Japanese industrial production, mining, textiles, and domestic agriculture from 1930 through August 1946. It includes extensive tables on commodity imports and exports, railway and water-borne transportation, manufacturing wages, and national debt. Comprehensive balance sheets for the Bank of Japan, the Deposit Bureau, and commercial banks document post-war currency changes and banking adjustments.
subfiles.title: Japanese Economic Statistics, Bulletin No. 1 (September 1946)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Official transmittal of five copies of SCAP Economic and Scientific Section Bulletin No. 1, 'Japanese Economic Statistics'.
subfiles.summary: Transmits five copies of SCAP's Japanese Economic Statistics Bulletin No. 1 to the Department of State.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 686 from United States Political Adviser, Tokyo, to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Student request from Birmingham, Alabama, for publications or pamphlets on Japanese economic conditions.
subfiles.summary: High school student requests pamphlets or papers on Japanese economic conditions for an upcoming class report.
subfiles.title: Letter from Dean Gaylor to State Department of Economics

subfiles.about: Department transmittal of two recent Far Eastern economic publications in response to student inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Transmits two recent Department publications on Far Eastern affairs to assist a student with an economic report.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. H. Fisher to Dean Gaylor

subfiles.about: Transmittal of draft sections of research study 'The Place of Foreign Trade in the Japanese Economy' for academic review.
subfiles.summary: Transmits drafts of Parts I and IV of Japanese foreign trade study to University of Denver professor for critique.
subfiles.title: Letter from Warren S. Hunsberger to Professor A. W. May

subfiles.about: Request for security clearance to send restricted Part II of Japanese foreign trade study to Professor James W. Angell.
subfiles.summary: Requests declassification clearance to transmit Part II of Japanese foreign trade study to Columbia University professor James W. Angell.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Warren S. Hunsberger to Harold Levin

subfiles.about: Security Office concurrence with transmitting restricted document OCL-2815, Part II, to Professor James W. Angell.
subfiles.summary: Confirms Security Office has no objection to transmitting restricted Japanese trade study Part II to Professor Angell.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Robert L. Bannerman to Division of Public Liaison

subfiles.about: Endorsement of research division request to provide restricted Japanese trade report Part II to Professor Angell.
subfiles.summary: Endorses recommendation to send restricted Japanese foreign trade study to Professor James W. Angell for critical review.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Paula H. Leland to Robert L. Bannerman

subfiles.about: Transmittal of State Department intelligence research report OCL-2815, Volume I, Part II, to Professor Angell.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Part II of State Department intelligence research report on Japanese trade to Professor Angell for comment.
subfiles.title: Letter from Walter Walkinshaw to Dr. James W. Angell

subfiles.about: Personal transmittal enclosing copy of Atcheson's confidential letter to President Truman on economic crisis in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards copy of personal report to President Truman concerning Japan's critical economic conditions and upcoming Washington consultations.
subfiles.title: Letter from George Atcheson, Jr. to James F. Byrnes

subfiles.about: Comprehensive political and economic assessment of occupied Japan, reviewing the new Constitution, inflation, labor unrest, and reparations.
subfiles.summary: Political Adviser George Atcheson reports to President Truman on occupation governance, the new Constitution, and defenses against leftist criticism of the Yoshida Cabinet. He details severe economic collapse, inflation, and communist influence in labor unions, stressing that Japan has become an American financial burden. Atcheson urges prompt resolution of reparations and revival of foreign trade so Japan can attain economic self-sufficiency.
subfiles.title: Letter from George Atcheson, Jr. to President Harry S. Truman

subfiles.about: Department transmittal of one copy of restricted study on Japanese foreign trade to the Chinese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Transmits one copy of restricted report on foreign trade in the Japanese economy to the Chinese Embassy.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Transmitting OCL-2815 to the Chinese Embassy

subfiles.about: Transmittal of SCAP message concerning Articles 21, 24, and 67 of Imperial House Economy Law for Committee No. 3.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SCAP message concerning Articles 21, 24, and 67 of Imperial House Economy Law to Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from J. H. Hilldring to Secretary General, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Summary of Moscow Pravda article by V. Iordansky criticizing the new Japanese constitution, rural landholders, and strike suppression.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Pravda article by V. Iordansky criticizing Japan's new constitution, rural conservative voting, and occupation labor restrictions.
subfiles.title: Telegram 6652 from Walter Bedell Smith to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Legal recommendations on draft SWNCC policy regarding dissolution of the Zaibatsu and compensation for foreign property interests.
subfiles.summary: Recommends framing Zaibatsu dissolution as security necessity under Japanese government authority and ensuring prompt compensation for United Nations and neutral nationals.
subfiles.title: Memorandum to Charles Fahy and Conrad E. Snow on Deconcentration Policy in Japan
subfiles.to: Charles Fahy and Conrad E. Snow
